content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: chat deflection on both queues, delayed breaks, general callback and cancelled late payments coaching — 80.4% service level for 09:45–15:30 at ₹3,687.","why":"Both queues are about 6–7 agents short because of absences (mostly bus-strike lateness, plus some sickness), while call volume is on forecast. This is a capacity gap, not a demand spike. With no action, service level for 09:45–15:30 is predicted at 68.3% with 6.8% abandons. P2 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target, at 80.4% overall and 4.4% abandons, with no policy breaches. It works by reducing calls: 20% of simple status and balance enquiries move to chat on both queues. Rest-of-day service level rises to 85.7%.","trade_offs":["Payments stays just under target at 78.5%, while general reaches 82.9%. The overall 80.4% clears the target by only a thin margin.","The free option, P1 (delayed breaks plus callback only), actually makes things worse: 65.9% service level and 7.2% abandons. It is not a real alternative.","P3 (payments overtime, ₹5,040) costs more but reaches only 74.3%, and general drops to 72.0%.","P4 (overtime on both queues plus deflection, ₹9,447) gives the most headroom: 86.2% service level and 3.1% abandons. It costs ₹5,760 more than P2.","P2 relies on customers accepting chat. Some customers will be moved off the phone, and cancelling the 15:30 payments coaching session costs development time."],"watch":"Watch whether chat deflection actually reaches the assumed 20% and how payments service level tracks against 78.5%. If deflection falls short or payments slips further, be ready to add overtime as in P4. Also check whether the strike-delayed staff arrive; if they do, the gap may close early and some actions could be stood down."}
